recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Adding separate markdown wording or restoring the old DSTU open-question note would duplicate current consolidated guidance and risk drift; any future elevation from SHOULD to SHALL should be handled by a new work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-9418 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU2 request to add guidance on character ranges for string and markdown datatypes: these datatypes SHOULD exclude character points below 32 except horizontal tab, carriage return, and line feed, with an open question about whether the SHOULD should later become SHALL.
initial_application: The request was initially applied in git-svn revision 7996, commit ed625d8f623ab0ecfdab565c84f657edaa77ede9, which added control-character notes for string and markdown and a DSTU open-question todo. That initial application contained the later-corrected u0010/u0013 notation errors.
additional_context: source/datatypes.html is the active datatype page via source/fhir.ini [type-pages]. Later related issues corrected and refined this text: FHIR-36679 fixed u0010/u0013 to u000D/u000A, FHIR-16940 clarified that markdown follows string rules, FHIR-38714 consolidated markdown guidance around the same string-rule model, FHIR-48953 added newline handling guidance, and a 2023 Zulip thread discussed implementation constraints around the SHOULD status without establishing a source change for this reconciliation.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source says strings SHOULD not contain Unicode character points below 32 except u0009, u000D, and u000A; recommends treating u000D, u000A, and u000D u000A as new lines; defines markdown as a FHIR string; and explicitly says markdown is subject to the same rules including valid characters.

related_jiras.note: Published clarification that markdown is subject to the same rules as string; already represented on the combined branch.
Published correction changed the erroneous u0010/u0013 notation inherited from the original application to u000D/u000A.
Published markdown clarification intentionally consolidated markdown's character restrictions under the rule that markdown is a string subject to the same rules.
Applied clarification added the current recommendation for treating u000D, u000A, and u000D u000A as new lines.
Published string serialization clarification relevant to unsupported Unicode character handling but not a separate decision for this seed.
